q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Uttar Pradesh?
q.x: Banawali is in Haryana; Hulas (Saharanpur), Sinauli (Baghpat, about 125 graves) and Mandi (Muzaffarnagar, a Late Harappan jewellery hoard) are in Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: The Harappan site of Hulas is located in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
q.x: Hulas is in Saharanpur district; Sinauli is in Baghpat and Mandi in Muzaffarnagar.

q.s: The earliest evidence of garlic in the Harappan civilisation comes from:
q.x: Balu in Haryana has yielded the earliest evidence of garlic; Lothal and Rangpur gave rice husk.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Indus seals?
o: Short lines of the Indus script
q.x: Indus seals were commonly of steatite, bore animal and Pashupati motifs and short lines of the undeciphered Indus script; Brahmi came much later.

q.s: The famous 'Pashupati' seal of the Harappan civilisation was found at:
q.x: The Pashupati (proto-Shiva) seal, showing a seated figure surrounded by animals, comes from Mohenjo-daro.

q.s: The 'Dancing Girl' figurine of Mohenjo-daro is made of:
q.x: The Dancing Girl is a bronze figure cast by the lost-wax process.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Harappan art object - material) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Male torso of Harappa - Red sandstone
q.x: The Mother Goddess figurines are of terracotta.

q.s: Which school of Indian philosophy was founded by Jaimini?
q.x: Jaimini founded Purva Mimamsa (the Karmakanda), which holds that liberation comes through ritual; Vaisheshika is Kanada's, Nyaya Gautama's and Sankhya Kapila's.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (school of philosophy - founder) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sankhya was founded by Kapila; Gautama founded Nyaya.

q.s: The Buddha compared his teaching to which of the following, to show that it was a means and not a dogma?
q.x: The Buddha likened his teaching to a raft used to cross the river and then left behind - a skilful means (upaya).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Buddha's teaching is correct?
o: He made belief in God a condition for entry into the Sangha.
He neither affirmed nor denied the existence of God.
He declared his teaching a fixed dogma to be held for ever.
He taught that liberation comes through Vedic sacrifice.
q.x: The Buddha was silent on God, did not require belief in God for Sangha membership and called his teaching a raft (upaya).

q.s: Buddhism is believed to have reached Andhra through the disciples of which sage of the Godavari region?
q.x: The disciples of sage Bavari, who lived on the Godavari, carried the Buddha's teaching to Andhra.

q.s: The three-month rainy-season retreat of Buddhist monks was called:
q.x: The Vassa was the rainy-season retreat; Pavarana marked its end, Uposatha was the fortnightly assembly and Pabbajja the initial ordination.

q.s: Odisha's Buddhist 'Diamond Triangle' is made up of Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and:
q.x: The Diamond Triangle is Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri; Dhauli and Jaugada are Ashokan rock-edict sites.

q.s: Megasthenes came to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra as the envoy of:
q.x: Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus I Nicator; Deimachus was later sent by Antiochus I to Bindusara.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Indica of Megasthenes is correct?
o: It was written in Sanskrit for the Mauryan court.
It was written by Deimachus, the envoy to Bindusara.
The original is lost and survives only in fragments quoted by later Greek and Roman writers.
Its complete original text has survived to the present day.
q.x: The Indica is lost; its fragments, quoted by Diodorus, Strabo, Pliny and Arrian, were compiled by Schwanbeck in 1846.

q.s: Arachosia, one of the provinces ceded by Seleucus to Chandragupta Maurya, corresponds to the present-day region of:
q.x: Arachosia is Kandahar; Aria is Herat, Paropanisadai is Kabul and Gedrosia is Balochistan.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the provinces ceded by Seleucus to Chandragupta Maurya?
q.x: Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Gedrosia and Paropanisadai; Bactria remained outside the Mauryan empire.

q.s: According to Megasthenes, the Mauryan army was administered by:
o: Five boards of six members each
Six boards of five members each
Four boards of eight members each
Eight boards of four members each
q.x: Megasthenes describes six boards of five members each for the army, one of them for the navy.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mauryan army, according to Megasthenes, is correct?
o: The army was run by a single commander without boards.
The navy was one of the boards of army administration.
q.x: One of the six boards looked after the navy; Chandragupta had 30,000 cavalry.

q.s: The Bhitari Pillar inscription records the war of which Gupta ruler against the Hunas?
q.x: The Bhitari Pillar of Skandagupta records his victory over the Hunas; the Junagadh inscription is also his.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (inscription - Gupta ruler) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Eran inscription of 510 CE belongs to Bhanugupta.

q.s: Which invaders blocked the north-western trade route and cut the inflow of gold and silver into Gupta India?
q.x: The Huna invasions blocked the north-western route and cut the inflow of gold and silver.

q.s: India's silk trade with the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire declined around 550 CE mainly because:
o: The Romans learnt to rear silkworms
The Hunas blocked the sea routes
q.x: The Byzantine silk and spice trade lasted till about 550 CE and ended when the Romans learnt sericulture.

q.s: Which Chalukya ruler entered Kanchi around 740 CE, spared the city and gave gold to the Kailasanatha (Rajasimheshvara) temple?
q.x: Vikramaditya II did not plunder Kanchi; he gave gold to the Rajasimheshvara (Kailasanatha) temple.

q.s: Alauddin Khalji's Gujarat campaign of 1299 was led by:
q.x: Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan led the 1299 Gujarat campaign.

q.s: Kamala Devi, captured during Alauddin Khalji's Gujarat campaign, was a queen of which dynasty?
q.x: Kamala Devi was the queen of the Vaghela ruler Karna of Gujarat; she later married Alauddin.

q.s: Who recaptured Warangal from the Tughlaqs in 1336?
q.x: Kapaya Nayaka of the Musunuri family recaptured Warangal; Prolaya Vema Reddi freed coastal Andhra and founded the Reddi kingdom.

q.s: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 by:
q.x: Hasan Gangu took the title Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah; Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah founded the Madurai Sultanate (1335).

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, the province (iqta) was governed by the:
q.x: The iqta (province) was under the muqti or wali; the amil and chaudhri worked in the smaller pargana.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, the official in charge of revenue collection in the pargana was the:
q.x: The amil collected revenue in the pargana; the barid was the intelligence officer.

q.s: Al-Biruni wrote his Kitab-ul-Hind in which language?
q.x: Al-Biruni of Khwarazm wrote Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind) in Arabic around 1030.

q.s: Al-Biruni, who came to India in the time of Mahmud of Ghazni, was a native of:
q.x: Al-Biruni was born in Khwarazm, in present-day Uzbekistan.

q.s: Aurangzeb, as Mughal viceroy of the Deccan, attacked Golconda in 1656 at the urging of:
q.x: Mir Jumla, the Golconda noble who went over to the Mughals, urged Aurangzeb's 1656 attack on Golconda.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four subas of the Mughal Deccan under Shah Jahan?
q.x: The four subas were Khandesh, Berar, Telangana and Daulatabad; Golconda was still a Qutb Shahi kingdom.

q.s: In the Mughal pargana, the Shiqdar was the:
q.x: The Shiqdar was the executive and police officer; the Potdar was the treasurer, the Bitikchi the accountant and the Qanungo the hereditary record-keeper.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Mughal pargana official - function) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Potdar (Khazanadar) was the treasurer; the Amil collected revenue and the Qanungo was a hereditary officer.

q.s: Machilipatnam, the first European centre in Andhra, was established in 1605 by the:
q.x: The Dutch set up at Machilipatnam in 1605; the English came there in 1611.

q.s: The famous diamonds of the Golconda region in the early modern period came mainly from the mines at:
q.x: Diamonds came from the Kollur mines on the Krishna; Motupalli was a port.

q.s: The capital of Banda Bahadur's Sikh state was:
q.x: Banda Bahadur made Lohgarh his capital and struck coins in the names of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh.

q.s: The Dal Khalsa, the combined force of the Sikh misls, was organised by:
q.x: Nawab Kapur Singh organised the Dal Khalsa; Bhai Mani Singh healed the Bandai-Tat Khalsa split.

q.s: The Taj Mahal is built mainly of:
q.x: The Taj Mahal is of white marble and its tomb stands at the river end of the charbagh; red sandstone marks Humayun's tomb.

q.s: Which of the following Mughal monuments is NOT built mainly of red sandstone?
q.x: The Taj Mahal is of white marble; the others are mainly red sandstone.

q.s: The Hamzanama, a Mughal illustrated manuscript of about 1,400 paintings, was completed under the supervision of:
q.x: The Hamzanama was begun under Mir Sayyid Ali and completed under Abdus Samad over about 15 years.

q.s: The Tarikh-i-Alfi, compiled at Akbar's court, is a history of:
o: The first thousand years of Islam
q.x: Tarikh-i-Alfi ('history of a thousand years') covers the first millennium of Islam.

q.s: Akbar's translation department, the Maktab Khana, was set up at:
q.x: The Maktab Khana at Fatehpur Sikri worked under Faizi.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Persian work - author) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Anwar-i-Suhaili is by Mulla Husain Waiz Kashifi; Abul Fazl made the Ayar-i-Danish.

q.s: Vyasa Tirtha, Rajaguru of Saluva Narasimha and Krishnadevaraya, belonged to which school of Vedanta?
q.x: Vyasa Tirtha was a Dvaita (Madhva) scholar; Shuddhadvaita was Vallabhacharya's school.

q.s: Surdas was a disciple of:
q.x: Surdas was Vallabhacharya's disciple; Sena was Ramananda's, Mirabai Raidas's and Janabai Namdev's.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (guru - disciple) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Janabai was Namdev's disciple; Sena the barber was Ramananda's.

q.s: Dasbodh was written by:
q.x: Dasbodh is the work of Samarth Ramdas.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (work - author) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Bijak is Kabir's; Kavitavali is Tulsidas's.

q.s: Madhura Vijayam, describing Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai, was written by:
q.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, wrote the Madhura Vijayam.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (work - woman poet) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Madhura Vijayam is Gangadevi's; Mohanangi, Krishnadevaraya's daughter, wrote Marichi Parinayam.

q.s: The followers of Basava are known as:
q.x: Basava's followers are the Lingayats (Virashaivas).

q.s: The Pashupata sect of Shaivism was founded by:
q.x: Lakulisha founded Pashupata Shaivism; Matsyendranath is linked with the Nathpanth.

q.s: The Dutch set up their factory at Surat in:
q.x: The Dutch came to Surat in 1616; the English were at Surat in 1613 and the French in 1668.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (European factory - year) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The French came to Surat in 1668.

q.s: The First Carnatic War was ended by the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended both the War of Austrian Succession and the First Carnatic War.

q.s: Under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748), Madras was returned to the English in exchange for:
q.x: Madras was exchanged for Louisbourg in North America, not Quebec.

q.s: Which Nawab of Arcot marched against the French after they took Madras in 1746, and was defeated at Adyar?
q.x: Anwaruddin, Nawab of Arcot from 1744, was defeated by the French at Adyar (St. Thome).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the First Carnatic War is correct?
o: Its immediate cause was the seizure of French ships by the English navy under Barnet.
It was ended by the Treaty of Paris.
Anwaruddin fought on the side of the French.
The English captured Pondicherry during the war.
q.x: Barnet's seizure of French ships started it; Anwaruddin opposed the French after they took Madras; the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ended it.

q.s: In the Battle of Buxar (1764), the British forces were commanded by:
q.x: Hector Munro led the British at Buxar in Bihar.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the rulers defeated by the British at Buxar?
q.x: Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-daula and Shah Alam II were defeated at Buxar; Siraj-ud-daula had lost at Plassey in 1757.

q.s: The Samp Sabha (1883) among the Bhils was founded by:
q.x: Govind Giri founded the Samp Sabha; Motilal Tejawat led the Eki movement (1921-22).

q.s: The Mangarh massacre of 1913, called the 'Adivasi Jallianwala', is associated with which tribe?
q.x: The Mangarh massacre of 17 November 1913 killed Bhil followers of Govind Giri.

q.s: The anicut across the Godavari at Dowleswaram was built under:
q.x: Sir Arthur Cotton built the Dowleswaram anicut (1846-52); the Krishna anicut was built under Charles Orr.

q.s: Which famine convinced the East India Company of the need for irrigation works in coastal Andhra?
q.x: The Guntur famine of 1833 led to the Godavari and Krishna anicuts.

q.s: The Madrasa-e-Aliya in Hyderabad (1873), meant for the sons of nobles, was founded by:
q.x: Salar Jung I founded the Madrasa-e-Aliya; it later merged into Nizam College (1887), whose principal was Aghorenath Chattopadhyaya.

q.s: The Charter Act of 1813 set aside how much a year for education in India?
q.x: The Charter Act of 1813 provided Rs 1 lakh a year for reviving literature and promoting science.

q.s: The General Committee of Public Instruction was set up in:
q.x: The GCPI was set up in 1823, when the 1813 grant was actually first made available.

q.s: The Brahmo Sabha was founded by Raja Rammohan Roy in:
q.x: The Brahmo Sabha dates from 1828; 1815 is the Atmiya Sabha and 1839 the Tattvabodhini Sabha.

q.s: Which of the following reform bodies was established last?
q.x: Order: Brahmo Sabha (1828), Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839), Arya Samaj (1875), Ramakrishna Mission (1897).

q.s: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by:
q.x: Atmaram Pandurang founded it under Keshab Chandra Sen's influence; Ranade joined in 1870 and became its chief mentor.

q.s: The Poona Pact (1932) reserved how many seats for the depressed classes in the provincial legislatures?
q.x: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates with 148 reserved seats in joint electorates, against 71 under the Communal Award.

q.s: Dr. Ambedkar's mass conversion to Buddhism on 14 October 1956 took place at:
q.x: The conversion at Deeksha Bhoomi, Nagpur was accompanied by 22 vows; Chaitya Bhoomi is his cremation site.

q.s: 'Sutapuranam' and 'Sambuka Vadha', which attacked caste and priestly dominance, were written by:
q.x: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary wrote these rationalist works; his song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' belongs to the Civil Disobedience Movement.

q.s: Gurajada Appa Rao was patronised by the court of:
q.x: Gurajada served the Vizianagaram court under Ananda Gajapati.

q.s: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy, leader of the spoken-Telugu (vyavaharika) movement, prepared a grammar of the language of which tribe?
q.x: Gidugu, who taught at Parlakimidi, wrote a Savara manual (1931) in English and received the Kaisar-e-Hind in 1934.

q.s: The Poona Seva Sadan (1909) was founded by Ramabai Ranade along with:
q.x: Ramabai Ranade and G.K. Devadhar founded the Poona Seva Sadan for women's education and welfare.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (organisation - founder) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Deva Samaj (Lahore, 1887) was founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri; Dayanand founded the Arya Samaj.

q.s: Dr. Ambedkar's 'broken men' theory of the origin of untouchability is set out in:
q.x: The Untouchables (1948) put forward the 'broken men' theory; Who Were the Shudras? (1946) argued the Shudras were originally Kshatriyas.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (work of Dr. Ambedkar - theme) is NOT correctly matched?
o: The Untouchables - Shudras were originally Kshatriyas
Who Were the Shudras? - Shudras were originally Kshatriyas
The Buddha and His Dhamma - Basis of Navayana
q.x: The Untouchables (1948) gives the 'broken men' theory of untouchability.

q.s: The Theosophical Society won wide acceptance among educated Hindus mainly because it:
o: Rejected the authority of the Vedas
Glorified ancient Hindu religion and philosophy
Advocated armed revolt against British rule
q.x: Its praise of the Vedas, Upanishads and ancient Hindu philosophy appealed to educated Hindus.

q.s: Which Viceroy dismissed the Indian National Congress in 1888 as representing a 'microscopic minority'?
q.x: Dufferin, after first tolerating the Congress, called it a 'microscopic minority'; A.O. Hume, not Dufferin, founded it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the founding of the Indian National Congress is correct?
o: Lord Dufferin himself founded the Congress.
Its first session was held at Calcutta.
Its first President was Dadabhai Naoroji.
A.O. Hume persuaded Lord Dufferin not to obstruct the new body.
q.x: Hume founded it with Dufferin's tolerance; the first session was at Bombay (1885) under W.C. Bonnerjee.

q.s: The Purna Swaraj resolution of the Indian National Congress was adopted at its 1929 session held at:
q.x: The Lahore session of 1929 under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted Purna Swaraj.

q.s: The Karachi session of the Congress (1931), which adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme, was presided over by:
q.x: Vallabhbhai Patel presided at Karachi, which endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution.

q.s: Who presided over the Madras session of the Indian National Congress in 1927?
q.x: M.A. Ansari presided at Madras in 1927; Motilal Nehru presided at Amritsar (1919) and Calcutta (1928).

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Congress President - session) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided at Jaipur in 1948.

q.s: In the Madras Presidency, the Swadeshi movement was led by:
q.x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai led Swadeshi in Madras; Syed Haider Raza led it in Delhi and Ajit Singh in Punjab.

q.s: Which of the following leaders was NOT associated with the Swadeshi movement in Bengal?
q.x: Ajit Singh led the movement in Punjab along with Lala Lajpat Rai.

q.s: Lala Lajpat Rai wrote 'Unhappy India' (1928) as a reply to:
o: James Mill's History of British India
q.x: Unhappy India answered Katherine Mayo's Mother India; Lajpat Rai also started Young India (1916, USA) and The People (1920).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a journal or work of Lala Lajpat Rai?
q.x: Kesari was Tilak's paper; Lajpat Rai started Young India (1916, USA) and The People (1920) and wrote Unhappy India (1928).

q.s: In the Alipore Bomb Case, Aurobindo Ghosh was defended by:
q.x: C.R. Das defended Aurobindo, who was acquitted in 1909; he retired to Pondicherry in 1910.

q.s: Aurobindo Ghosh's series of articles 'New Lamps for Old' appeared in:
q.x: 'New Lamps for Old' was published in the Indu Prakash of Bombay in 1893-94.

q.s: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was formed in September 1928 at:
q.x: The HSRA was formed at Ferozshah Kotla, Delhi; the original HRA had been founded at Kanpur in 1924.

q.s: The first all-India hartal against the Rowlatt Act was observed on:
q.x: The hartal of 6 April 1919 was the first all-India mass strike; Gandhi withdrew the satyagraha on 18 April after violence.

q.s: The Rowlatt Act, passed in March 1919 despite the opposition of every Indian member of the Imperial Legislative Council, was repealed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The Rowlatt Act was repealed under Lord Reading (1921-26), along with the Press Act, 1910; Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in protest when it was passed.

q.s: Which Andhra leader was given the title 'Andhra Ratna'?
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was Andhra Ratna; Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary was Andhra Sivaji.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (title - leader) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Andhra Sivaji was Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary.

q.s: The Bhoodan movement was launched by Vinoba Bhave on 18 April 1951 at:
q.x: Bhoodan began at Pochampalli in Telangana; landlords were asked to give at least one-sixth of their land.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Bhoodan and Sarvodaya is correct?
o: Landlords were asked to give half of their land.
Sarvodaya Day is observed on 30 January.
Dr. Ambedkar praised the village as the ideal basic unit of the Constitution.
q.x: Bhoodan began at Pochampalli, asked for one-sixth of the land, and Ambedkar called the village 'a sink of localism'.

q.s: In the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra, the organisation of district 'dictators', war councils and camps (sibirams) is credited to:
q.x: The district dictator-war council-sibiram scheme was Pattabhi Sitaramayya's idea.

q.s: India chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission in Korea (1953) under:
q.x: Gen. K.S. Thimayya headed the NNRC in Korea.

q.s: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally founded in 1961 at:
q.x: NAM's first summit was at Belgrade in 1961; the Bandung Conference (1955) was sponsored by the Colombo Powers.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Second Five Year Plan is correct?
o: It gave top priority to agriculture and irrigation.
It was followed by a period of food surplus and falling prices.
It was based on the Mahalanobis model and gave priority to heavy industry.
q.x: The Second Plan's heavy-industry priority came at the cost of agriculture, leading to food shortages and inflation; the rolling plan came in 1978-80.

q.s: Under the Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950, how many years of cultivation made a tenant a 'protected tenant'?
q.x: Six years' cultivation gave protected-tenant status with hereditary rights; the price of ownership could be paid in 20 instalments.

q.s: The JVP Committee on linguistic provinces (1948) consisted of Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and:
q.x: The JVP Committee - Jawaharlal, Vallabhbhai, Pattabhi - was set up at the Jaipur session (1948).

q.s: The JVP Committee said that a separate Andhra province could be considered if the Andhras:
o: Accepted Telugu as the only official language
Merged with Hyderabad State at once
Agreed to a Union Territory for Madras
Gave up their claim to Madras city
q.x: The JVP report made the Andhra state conditional on giving up the claim to Madras.

q.s: Who moved the resolution on linguistic provinces in the Imperial Legislative Council in 1918?
q.x: B.N. Sarma moved the 1918 resolution; Jinnah and Srinivasa Sastri opposed it and Rangaswami Ayyangar supported it.

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission (1953-55) was headed by:
q.x: Fazl Ali chaired the SRC; H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were members, and S.K. Dhar headed the 1948 commission.

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission recommended that Telangana should initially function as a separate state called:
q.x: The SRC (para 386) proposed Telangana as Hyderabad State, with merger after the 1961 elections if two-thirds of its legislators agreed.

q.s: AMS dates of about 2100 BCE from Mayiladumparai indicate that the Iron Age in South India began:
o: Later than in the Gangetic valley
At the same time as in the Gangetic valley
Earlier than in the Gangetic valley
q.x: The Mayiladumparai dates push the South Indian Iron Age earlier than the Gangetic Iron Age.

q.s: The megalithic site of Jonnawada is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Jonnawada is in Nellore district, not Kurnool.

q.s: Which of the following dynasties succeeded the Satavahanas in Andhra?
q.x: The Ikshvakus ruled Andhra; the Abhiras took Maharashtra, the Chutus Karnataka and the Vakatakas Vidarbha.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a successor state of the Satavahanas?
q.x: The Ikshvakus, Abhiras, Chutus, Pallavas and Vakatakas followed the Satavahanas; the Kakatiyas rose about a thousand years later.

q.s: Which of the following was imported from China in the Satavahana period?
q.x: Silk and camphor came from China, while muslin, pearls, spices, diamonds and ivory were exported.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an export of the Satavahana period?
q.x: Wine was imported from Italy and Arabia; muslin, pearls and spices were exported.

q.s: The Buddhist site of Amaravati was identified in 1797 by:
q.x: Colin Mackenzie, later the first Surveyor General of India, identified Amaravati; Fergusson wrote on its sculptures in 'Tree and Serpent Worship'.

q.s: 'Sriparvata', mentioned in early Andhra inscriptions, is identified with:
q.x: Sriparvata is identified with Nagarjunakonda, the Ikshvaku capital region.

q.s: The Chuladhammagiri vihara at Nagarjunakonda, built by Bodhisri, was meant for monks from:
q.x: Chuladhammagiri, Bodhisri's Sinhala vihara, housed Theravada (Mahaviharavasin) monks from Sri Lanka.

q.s: The Vishnukundin dynasty was founded by:
q.x: Indravarma, a Vakataka vassal, founded the dynasty and built Indrapalanagara.

q.s: The last Vishnukundin ruler, Manchana Bhattaraka, was defeated by:
q.x: Pulakesin II defeated Manchana Bhattaraka around 624 CE, after which the Eastern Chalukyas took over coastal Andhra.

q.s: The Vishnukundin ruler Govinda Varma I bore the title:
q.x: Govinda Varma I, who expanded into the Krishna-Godavari region, was Shadabhigna; Vishamasiddhi was Kubja Vishnuvardhana's title.

q.s: The Janasraya Chhandovichiti, associated with the Vishnukundins, is a work on:
q.x: Janasraya Chhandovichiti is a treatise on prosody (chhandas), credited to Madhava Varma II or the poet Gunaswami.

q.s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler reigned between Kirtivarman I and Pulakesin II?
q.x: The order is Pulakesin I, Kirtivarman I, Mangalesha, Pulakesin II and later Vikramaditya I.

q.s: Chellavva, who received the village Attili from Chalukya Bhima I and bore the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada, was famous as a:
q.x: Gandharva-vidya means music; the Attili inscription records the grant to her.

q.s: Hallisaka, a popular dance of the Eastern Chalukya period, is identified with:
q.x: Hallisaka, a circular group dance, is identified with Kolatam.

q.s: Bhairavakona, with eight rock-cut Shiva cave temples, lies in which hills?
q.x: Bhairavakona is in the Nallamala hills of Prakasam district.

q.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, a Vishaya or Mandala was headed by the:
q.x: The state was divided into Vishayas or Mandalas under a Vishayapati or Mandaleswara.

q.s: The Renati Cholas claimed descent from:
q.x: The Renati Cholas called themselves Suryavamsa Kshatriyas of Karikala's line; their Renadu was 'Saptasahasra' (7,000 villages).

q.s: Ranganatha Ramayanam is regarded as the earliest Telugu work in which literary form?
q.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is the earliest dwipada kavya; Sugriva Vijayam is a Yakshagana.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (literary form - example) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sugriva Vijayam is a Yakshagana; Ranganatha Ramayanam is the earliest dwipada kavya.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a seat of the Reddi kings?
q.x: The Reddis ruled from Addanki, then Kondavidu, with Rajahmundry as a second seat (1402-1448); Warangal was the Kakatiya capital.

q.s: Bhrugupatham, the practice of leaping from a hill as a religious offering, was associated with:
q.x: Bhrugupatham was practised at Srisailam; Champudu Gullu was at Tripurantakam.

q.s: Which Bahmani Sultan had the Musunuri prince Vinayaka Deva burnt alive in 1361?
q.x: Muhammad Shah I burnt Vinayaka alive; later Gajarao Tippa defeated Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta (1396).

q.s: Robert Sewell's 'A Forgotten Empire' (1900) contains translations of the accounts of which visitors to Vijayanagara?
q.x: Sewell translated the chronicles of Paes and Nuniz, the latter a Portuguese horse trader.

q.s: Which of the following is a local (indigenous) literary source for Vijayanagara history?
q.x: Amuktamalyada and the Rayavachakam are local Telugu sources; Firishta wrote from the Deccan Sultanate side.

q.s: Who succeeded Ganapatideva on the Kakatiya throne in 1262?
q.x: Rudramadevi succeeded Ganapatideva; Prataparudra came after her.

q.s: The last Kakatiya ruler was:
q.x: Prataparudra, Rudramadevi's grandson and successor, was defeated by the Tughlaqs in 1323.

q.s: Radhakrishna Dandasena's rising at Parlakimidi in 1857 was a rising of which tribe?
q.x: Dandasena led a Savara rising at Parlakimidi.

q.s: Korukonda Subba Reddy of the Godavari region rose in 1857 on rumours of the advancing army of:
q.x: Subba Reddy rose on rumours of Nana Saheb's army; the British put him down with the help of the Buttaigudem Munsab Shankar Swamy.

q.s: In 1952 the Andhra communists started which daily at Vijayawada after their organ Prajasakti had been banned?
q.x: With Prajasakti banned in 1948, Visalandhra was started at Vijayawada on 22 June 1952.

q.s: The zamindari system in the Madras Presidency was abolished by the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act of:
q.x: The Madras Estates Land Act, 1908 only regulated landholder-ryot relations; abolition came in 1948.

q.s: Which Telugu poet was given the title 'Kavi Samrat'?
q.x: Kavi Samrat is Viswanatha Satyanarayana; Maha Kavi is Sri Sri and Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti is Gurram Jashuva.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (title - poet) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Abhyudaya Kavitha Pitamahudu is Gurajada Apparao.

q.s: Which Telugu play was banned by the Andhra Pradesh government in January 2022 over its portrayal of the character Subbi Setty?
q.x: The ban on staging Chintamani followed objections to the depiction of Subbi Setty.

q.s: In his early years Tanguturi Prakasam acted in main roles with the Hindu Nataka Samajam of:
q.x: Prakasam acted with the Hindu Nataka Samajam, Rajahmundry; Bellary was the base of Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao and Bellary Raghava.

q.s: Ponaka Kanakamma is known for leading the anti-zamindari struggle in which district?
q.x: Ponaka Kanakamma of Nellore led the anti-zamindari struggle and founded schools.

q.s: The Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937) was founded by:
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh, who also led the Salt Satyagraha in Madras city, founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha.

q.s: Kondapalli toys are made from which light wood?
q.x: Kondapalli toys (NTR district) are carved from the soft Tella Poniki wood.

q.s: The freehand, pen-drawn style of Kalamkari is associated with:
q.x: Srikalahasti Kalamkari is freehand pen work; Machilipatnam-Pedana is block-printed, and Etikoppaka is known for lacquerware toys.

q.s: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on:
q.x: The flag was adopted on 22 July 1947, with the Ashoka Chakra replacing the charkha; the anthem and song were adopted on 24 January 1950.

q.s: Jana Gana Mana was first sung at which session of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: Jana Gana Mana was first sung at the Calcutta session of 1911.

q.s: According to T.K. Oommen's study of urban families, joint families with strong elder-male authority are found mainly in the:
q.x: Oommen classified urban families by livelihood, authority structure, social milieu and values; the proprietary class kept joint families under elder-male authority.

q.s: Dr. Ambedkar's paper 'Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development' (1916) was presented at:
q.x: Ambedkar read 'Castes in India' at an anthropology seminar at Columbia University in 1916.

q.s: According to B.S. Guha's racial classification, the Jarawa and Onge of the Andaman Islands belong to the:
q.x: Guha placed the Jarawa and Onge among the Negritos; Risley's separate scheme spoke of Dravidian and Mongoloid types.

q.s: Which law gives women a 'Right to Residence' in the shared household?
o: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
q.x: Section 17 of the Domestic Violence Act, a civil remedy, gives the Right to Residence.

q.s: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to:
q.x: Muslims follow their personal law and Hindus, Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists the Hindu Succession Act.

q.s: The Women's Indian Association was founded in:
q.x: The WIA dates from 1917; the Bharat Stree Mahamandal from 1910, the NCWI from 1925 and the Andhra Mahila Sabha from 1937.

q.s: Which is regarded as India's first women's organisation, founded in 1910?
o: National Council of Women in India
q.x: Sarala Devi Chaudhurani's Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910) is regarded as the first.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court in 1985 uphold a divorced Muslim woman's right to maintenance under Section 125 CrPC?
q.x: Shah Bano (1985) was followed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.

q.s: Instant triple talaq was held unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 2017 in:
q.x: In Shayara Bano (3:2) the majority was formed by Justices Nariman, Lalit and Joseph.

q.s: The proviso to Article 164(1), requiring a Minister in charge of tribal welfare, applies to Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and:
q.x: The proviso covers Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP and Odisha; that Minister may also hold SC and BC welfare.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment removed Bihar from the proviso to Article 164(1) and added Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand?
q.x: The 94th Amendment (2006) made the change.

q.s: Under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, offences are:
q.x: Offences are cognizable and non-bailable; the Act bans insanitary latrines and hazardous manual cleaning of sewers by anyone, contractors included.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 is correct?
o: It permits hazardous cleaning when done through private contractors.
It bans hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, even through contractors.
It allows insanitary latrines in rural areas.
q.x: The Act, in force from 6 December 2013, bans insanitary latrines and hazardous cleaning by anyone; offences are cognizable and non-bailable.

q.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, an honour killing is prosecuted as murder under Section:
q.x: Section 103 punishes murder; Section 69 covers intercourse by deceitful means and Section 70 gang rape.

q.s: Courts in India have read the Right to Food into which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: The Right to Food is part of the Right to Life under Article 21.

q.s: Who defined public policy as 'a purposive course of action followed by an actor or set of actors in dealing with a problem'?
q.x: The definition is James Anderson's; Thomas Dye called policy 'whatever governments choose to do or not to do'.

q.s: Which of the following statements about unemployment in India is correct?
o: Disguised unemployment is mainly found in the urban labour market.
Educated unemployment is predominantly a rural phenomenon.
Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in agriculture.
Frictional unemployment is mainly found on family farms.
q.x: Seasonal unemployment is agricultural; disguised unemployment is found mainly on family farms, while educated and frictional unemployment are urban.

q.s: The Rangarajan Expert Group on poverty measurement (2012) was set up by the:
q.x: The Planning Commission set it up; NITI Aayog came only in 2015.

q.s: The Rangarajan poverty line for rural areas in 2011-12 was about how much per person per day?
q.x: Rangarajan put the line at Rs 32 a day rural and Rs 47 urban (Rs 972 and Rs 1,407 a month); Tendulkar's was about Rs 27 and Rs 33.

q.s: Who became the Minister for Women and Child Welfare of Andhra Pradesh in the government formed in June 2024?
q.x: Gummadi Sandhya Rani holds Women and Child Welfare since 12 June 2024; Taneti Vanitha was Home Minister in the earlier government.

q.s: 'Invalidity and old age pensions' is an entry in which List of the Seventh Schedule?
o: None; it is a residuary subject
q.x: Old age pensions fall in Entry 24 of the Concurrent List; the NSAP rests on Articles 41 and 42.

q.s: The first State law for the maintenance of parents was enacted in 2001 by:
q.x: Himachal Pradesh's 2001 law came before the central Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007.

q.s: The National Commission for Minorities became a statutory body under the Act passed in:
q.x: The non-statutory Minorities Commission (1978) became statutory under the NCM Act, 1992.

q.s: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was carved out of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in:
q.x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was created in 2006.

q.s: Under Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, minority communities are notified by the:
o: President after a resolution of Parliament
q.x: Minorities under the NCM Act are those notified by the Central Government; the Constitution itself does not define 'minority'.

q.s: Following the T.M.A. Pai case (2002), minority status for the purpose of Article 30 is determined with reference to:
q.x: T.M.A. Pai held that linguistic and religious minorities are to be determined State-wise.

q.s: India's military response to the Pahalgam terror attack of April 2025 was code-named:
q.x: Operation Sindoor followed Pahalgam (22 April 2025), and the Indus Waters Treaty was put in abeyance; Parakram followed the 2001 Parliament attack.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (terror attack - India's response) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Uri was answered by surgical strikes across the LoC; Balakot followed Pulwama.

q.s: The Mangdechhu hydroelectric project (720 MW), built with Indian help, is located in:
q.x: Mangdechhu (inaugurated 2019) and the Punatsangchhu projects are in Bhutan.

q.s: The 1949 India-Bhutan Treaty of Friendship was revised, dropping the clause on Indian guidance in foreign affairs, in:
q.x: The 2007 revision removed the clause that Bhutan be guided by India in its foreign relations.

q.s: The first India-US 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue was held in:
q.x: The 2+2 began in 2018; the Strategic and Commercial Dialogue in 2015 and Quad leaders' summits in 2021.

q.s: The UAE was the first foreign investor in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve located at:
q.x: ADNOC of the UAE took space in the Mangaluru SPR; the UAE is also India's second-largest source of remittances after the USA.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)?
q.x: The GCC has six members: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman.

q.s: Who has been the Director-General of the International Labour Organization since 2022?
q.x: Gilbert Houngbo succeeded Guy Ryder in 2022; Audrey Azoulay headed UNESCO.

q.s: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus is the Director-General of which organisation?
q.x: Tedros heads the WHO, in a second term to August 2027.

q.s: The first allocation of Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) by the IMF was made in:
q.x: SDRs were created in 1967-69 and first allocated in 1970.

q.s: The IMF and the IBRD were conceived at the Bretton Woods conference held in:
q.x: Bretton Woods met in July 1944; the IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945.

q.s: The SAARC Secretariat is located at:
q.x: The SAARC Charter was signed at Dhaka (8 December 1985); the Secretariat is at Kathmandu.

q.s: Which country joined SAARC in 2007 as its eighth member?
q.x: Afghanistan joined in 2007; the Maldives and Bhutan were founder members.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the G7?
q.x: India is only an invited outreach partner; Russia, part of the G8 from 1997-98, was suspended in 2014 after Crimea.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's maritime doctrines is correct?
o: MAHASAGAR (2025) widens SAGAR to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South.
SHANTI is India's security framework for the Arabian Sea.
SAGAR stands for 'Security and Governance Across Regions'.
q.x: SAGAR (2015) is Security and Growth for All in the Region; MAHASAGAR (2025) extends it; SHANTI covers the Bay of Bengal.

q.s: The Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA), enacted in 2002, was repealed in:
q.x: POTA was repealed in 2004 and its key provisions moved into the UAPA.

q.s: The amendment to the UAPA that allowed individuals to be designated as terrorists was made in:
q.x: The 2019 UAPA amendment permitted designation of individuals as terrorists.

q.s: Who described Indian federalism as 'bargaining federalism'?
q.x: Morris-Jones used 'bargaining federalism'; Wheare called India 'quasi-federal' and Austin 'cooperative federalism'.

q.s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'a federation with a strong centralising tendency'?
q.x: The phrase is Ivor Jennings's; H.V. Kamath spoke of the Constitution's 'elephantine size'.

q.s: Financial Emergency is provided for under which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 360 is Financial Emergency; 352 is National Emergency and 356 President's Rule.

q.s: Which of the following Articles is NOT part of the Emergency Provisions (Part XVIII) of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 368, on amendment, is in Part XX.

q.s: The word 'secular' was added to the Preamble of the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity'; Indian secularism means equal respect and principled distance, not complete separation.

q.s: The right to freedom of religion is guaranteed under which Articles of the Constitution?
q.x: Articles 25-28 deal with freedom of religion; 29-30 are cultural and educational rights.

q.s: A person born in India on or after 3 December 2004 is a citizen by birth only if:
o: Both parents are citizens, or one is a citizen and the other is not an illegal migrant
At least one parent is a citizen, whatever the other's status
He is born on Indian soil, whatever the parents' nationality
Both parents have lived in India for at least ten years
q.x: From 3 December 2004 an illegal-migrant parent bars citizenship by birth; births between 1950 and 30 June 1987 conferred citizenship regardless of parentage.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that Parliament cannot abridge Fundamental Rights by a constitutional amendment?
q.x: Golaknath gave FRs a transcendental position; the 24th Amendment answered it with Article 13(4).

q.s: Which of the following pairs (case - holding) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Shankari Prasad - A constitutional amendment is not 'law' under Article 13
I.R. Coelho - Review of Ninth Schedule laws added after 24 April 1973
q.x: Golaknath held that Parliament cannot abridge Fundamental Rights; the basic structure doctrine came in Kesavananda.

q.s: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is available to foreigners as well as citizens?
q.x: Article 21 extends to all persons; Articles 15, 19 and 29 are for citizens only, so companies cannot claim Article 19.

q.s: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is NOT available to foreigners?
q.x: Article 19 freedoms are for citizens only; Articles 14, 20 and 21 apply to all persons.

q.s: When a private individual violates a person's rights under Article 19 or 21, the remedy normally available is:
o: A reference by the President under Article 143
q.x: Articles 19 and 21 are guarantees against the State, so violation by a private person is met by ordinary legal remedies, not a writ.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the creamy layer principle can be applied to SC/ST reservation in promotions?
q.x: Jarnail Singh (2018) applied creamy layer to SC/ST promotions; M. Nagaraj required quantifiable data for promotion quotas.

q.s: The Supreme Court first held that reservation should generally not exceed 50 per cent and that caste cannot be the sole test of backwardness in:
o: Ram Singh v. Union of India
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
q.x: Balaji (1962) set the 50 per cent ceiling; Ram Singh (2015) struck Jats out of the Central OBC list.

q.s: The 91st Amendment (2003) limited the size of the Council of Ministers to what percentage of the strength of the Lok Sabha / Assembly?
q.x: The 91st Amendment capped Ministers at 15 per cent and barred defectors from becoming Ministers.

q.s: The present Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) was added to the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 52nd Amendment added the anti-defection Tenth Schedule; the 35th had added an earlier Tenth Schedule on Sikkim's associate status.

q.s: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was rolled out in India from:
q.x: GST began on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Amendment, which also omitted Article 268A.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 246A, added by the 101st Amendment, is correct?
o: Parliament and the State Legislatures can both make GST laws, but inter-State supply is for Parliament alone.
Only Parliament can make laws on GST.
Only the State Legislatures can make laws on GST.
GST laws can be made only after a unanimous vote of the GST Council.
q.x: Article 246A gives concurrent power over GST with inter-State supply reserved to Parliament; the GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, decides by three-fourths weighted vote.

q.s: How many times can a person be re-elected to the office of Vice-President of India?
q.x: The Vice-President is eligible for re-election any number of times; as Rajya Sabha Chairman he has only a casting vote.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Vice-President of India is correct?
o: He presides over the Rajya Sabha even while a resolution for his own removal is considered.
He is elected by the members of both Houses and the State Legislative Assemblies.
As Chairman of the Rajya Sabha he has only a casting vote in case of a tie.
He can be re-elected only once.
q.x: The Vice-President is elected by the members of both Houses only, can be re-elected any number of times and does not preside during his removal.

q.s: Under which Article is all executive action of the Government of India expressed to be taken in the name of the President?
q.x: Article 77 covers the conduct of business in the President's name; Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice.

q.s: The duty of the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers is laid down in:
q.x: Article 78 lists the PM's duties to communicate decisions and furnish information.

q.s: After the bifurcation of 2014, how many Rajya Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have?
q.x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 split undivided AP's 18 Rajya Sabha seats into 11 for AP and 7 for Telangana.

q.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have after the bifurcation of 2014?
q.x: Undivided AP's 42 Lok Sabha seats became 25 for AP and 17 for Telangana; the AP Assembly has 175 seats.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the creation or abolition of Legislative Councils in the States?
q.x: Article 169 lets Parliament create or abolish a Council on a resolution of the State Assembly.

q.s: A law of Parliament creating or abolishing a State Legislative Council under Article 169 is passed by:
o: A special majority and ratification by half the States
Two-thirds of the total membership of each House
q.x: Article 169 says such a law is not an amendment for the purposes of Article 368, so a simple majority suffices.

q.s: The veto of the American President over a Bill can be overridden by the Congress by a:
q.x: The American President's veto is qualified - Congress can override it by two-thirds; the Indian President has an absolute veto.

q.s: The Indian President can exercise a 'pocket veto' because:
o: He can return a Bill any number of times
The Constitution sets no time limit for him to act on a Bill
He can refer any Bill to the Supreme Court
A Bill lapses if he does not sign it in ten days
q.x: With no time limit for assent, the President can keep a Bill pending indefinitely.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution gives the Attorney General of India the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament?
q.x: Under Article 88 the Attorney General can take part in proceedings but has no vote; Article 76 creates the office.

q.s: The power to pardon a sentence passed by a court martial belongs to the:
q.x: Only the President can pardon court-martial sentences under Article 72.

q.s: The pardoning power of the Governor is provided under:
q.x: Article 161 covers offences against laws on matters to which the State's executive power extends.

q.s: A person who is a 'distinguished jurist' qualifies for appointment as Attorney General if he is so in the opinion of the:
q.x: The AG must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge: 5 years as a High Court judge, 10 years as a High Court advocate, or a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion.

q.s: To qualify as Attorney General through practice, a person must have been an advocate of a High Court for at least:
q.x: Ten years as a High Court advocate is one route; the judge route is five years as a High Court judge.

q.s: The first law officer of the Government of India is the:
q.x: The Attorney General is the government's chief legal adviser and first law officer; the CJI heads the judiciary.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General of India is correct?
o: He is appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
He must be a member of Parliament.
The Constitution fixes his term of office at five years.
He can take part in the proceedings of Parliament but cannot vote.
q.x: The AG is appointed by the President, holds office during his pleasure, and has a right to speak in either House under Article 88 without a vote.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court uphold the validity of the anti-defection Tenth Schedule in 1992?
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
q.x: Kihoto Hollohan upheld the Tenth Schedule 3:2 and struck down Paragraph 7 for want of State ratification.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) is correct?
o: The Tenth Schedule was struck down as a whole.
It allowed judicial review of a Speaker's decision before the decision is made.
Paragraph 7 of the Tenth Schedule was struck down for want of ratification by the States.
q.x: The Court upheld the Tenth Schedule 3:2 and barred review before the Speaker decides.

q.s: Who proposed a presidential form of government for India in the 1970s and 1980s?
q.x: Vasant Sathe argued for a presidential system; the NCRWC under Venkatachaliah advised keeping the parliamentary system.

q.s: The salaries and pensions of the judges of the Supreme Court are charged on the:
q.x: Supreme Court judges' salaries and pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted.

q.s: The pension of a High Court judge is charged on the:
q.x: A High Court judge's salary is charged on the State's Consolidated Fund but his pension on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q.s: The High Court of Andhra State was first established in 1954 at:
q.x: The Andhra High Court began at Guntur in 1954 and moved to Hyderabad on 1 November 1956.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the High Court of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: It moved to Hyderabad on 1 November 1956 as the High Court of united Andhra Pradesh.
It was first set up at Kurnool in 1953.
AP and Telangana have had separate High Courts since 2 June 2014.
The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 itself named its principal seat.
q.x: The Andhra High Court began at Guntur in 1954; the common High Court at Hyderabad served both States till 31 December 2018, and the principal seat was left to a Presidential order.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh was placed under President's Rule in 1973 in the context of the:
q.x: The Jai Andhra agitation followed the Supreme Court's upholding of the Mulki rules (1972).

q.s: A proclamation of President's Rule under Article 356 must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within:
q.x: President's Rule needs approval within two months by a simple majority; a National Emergency needs approval within one month by a special majority.

q.s: Under which Article may the President hold that a State government cannot be carried on per the Constitution if it fails to comply with Union directions?
q.x: Article 365 links non-compliance with Union directions to Article 356; Article 256 requires States to comply with Parliament's laws.

q.s: Directions to the States under Article 257 relate to:
o: Means of communication and protection of railways
q.x: Article 257 directions cover communications of national or military importance and railways, not public order.

q.s: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, an Election Commissioner holds office for:
o: Five years or till 62 years of age
Six years or till 62 years of age
Five years or till 65 years of age
Six years or till 65 years of age
q.x: An EC holds office for six years or till 65, whichever is earlier, and cannot be reappointed; the Act is under challenge in Jaya Thakur v. Union of India.

q.s: The Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms (1974-75) was appointed by:
q.x: The Tarkunde Committee was a non-official committee set up by Jayaprakash Narayan.

q.s: The State Election Commissioner, who conducts panchayat and municipal elections, is appointed by the:
q.x: Under Article 243K the Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner.

q.s: In a district, the District Election Officer who appoints Returning and Presiding Officers is usually the:
q.x: The Collector is the DEO; the Chief Electoral Officer of a State is a statutory authority appointed by the ECI in consultation with the State.

q.s: The Director of the CBI is appointed on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India (or his nominee) and the:
o: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
q.x: The committee is PM, LoP (or leader of the largest opposition party) and CJI; the Director has a minimum two-year tenure, extendable up to five years.

q.s: The CBI's Director of Prosecution is appointed on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Director of Prosecution is appointed on the CVC's recommendation.

q.s: The Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations was appointed in:
q.x: The Punchhi Commission (2007) reported in 2010 with 273 recommendations; Sarkaria was 1983 and Rajamannar 1969.

q.s: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000) was headed by:
q.x: The NCRWC was set up by the Vajpayee government under Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT usually criticised as an instrument of central control against the federal principle?
q.x: The Governor, the All India Services and the Planning Commission are criticised as tools of central control; the Inter-State Council is a forum for cooperation.

q.s: Which of the following was a recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission (1983)?
o: The residuary power of taxation should be moved to the Concurrent List.
The Centre may deploy its armed forces in a State even without the State's request.
The division of work between the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission should be changed.
Article 356 should be deleted from the Constitution.
q.x: Sarkaria kept residuary taxation with Parliament, found the FC-PC division reasonable and wanted Article 356 used sparingly, not deleted.

q.s: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre-State relations was appointed by the government of:
q.x: The DMK government of M. Karunanidhi appointed it; Dr P.V. Rajamannar was a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court.

q.s: Which of the following bodies on Centre-State relations was NOT appointed by the Union Government?
q.x: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by the Tamil Nadu government; the others were Union bodies.

q.s: The preparation of electoral rolls and the allocation of seats are dealt with in the:
q.x: The RPA 1950 covers seats and electoral rolls; the RPA 1951 covers the conduct of elections, disqualifications, corrupt practices and election petitions.

q.s: Corrupt practices and election petitions are dealt with in the:
q.x: Disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes are in the RPA 1951.

q.s: Disputes relating to the election of the President of India are decided by the:
q.x: Under Article 71, Presidential election disputes are decided by the Supreme Court.

q.s: From 1 July 2024, electoral offences such as bribery and personation are dealt with in Chapter IX of the:
q.x: Electoral offences moved from the IPC to Chapter IX of the BNS.

q.s: The 'None of the Above' (NOTA) option in elections was introduced following the Supreme Court judgment in:
o: Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013)
q.x: PUCL (2013) gave NOTA; the VVPAT ruling was Subramanian Swamy v. ECI.

q.s: In N. Chandrababu Naidu v. Union of India (2019), the Supreme Court raised VVPAT-EVM verification to how many polling stations per Assembly segment?
q.x: The tally was raised from one to five polling stations; ADR v. ECI (2024) rejected a return to paper ballots.

q.s: The study team on Nyaya Panchayats (1962) was headed by:
q.x: G.R. Rajagopalan studied Nyaya Panchayats; K. Santhanam headed the committee on Panchayat elections (1965).

q.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended:
o: A two-tier system of Panchayati Raj
A three-tier system of Panchayati Raj
Abolition of the Community Development Programme
q.x: Balwant Rai Mehta proposed democratic decentralisation through three tiers; Ashok Mehta (1978) proposed two tiers.

q.s: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) in:
q.x: FEMA was enacted in 1999, not as part of the 1991 package.

q.s: Compulsory industrial licensing is still retained for all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Licensing is retained only for alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives and electronic aerospace and defence equipment.

q.s: The Jawahar Knowledge Centres of Andhra Pradesh, which trained college students in technical and soft skills, were run by the:
q.x: The JKCs were run by the IEG, a society under the IT&C Department.

q.s: Women's self-help groups in Andhra Pradesh are popularly known as:
q.x: AP's SHGs are called DWCRA groups; Kudumbashree is Kerala's and Jeevika Bihar's.

q.s: SAPAP (1995), on which Andhra Pradesh's Velugu programme was built, was supported by the:
q.x: SAPAP was a UNDP-supported project; Velugu is run by SERP, a society of the Rural Development Department.

q.s: Zero or minimum tillage helps save irrigation water mainly because it:
o: Reduces evaporation and keeps soil moisture
q.x: Undisturbed soil with crop-residue mulch cuts evaporation and retains moisture.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which district of the present Andhra Pradesh was the most populous?
q.x: East Godavari was the most populous; Visakhapatnam had the largest ST population and Chittoor the highest share of cultivators.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the least literate district of the present Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Vizianagaram had the lowest literacy rate in Census 2011.

q.s: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was to be the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for a period not exceeding:
q.x: The common-capital period ran till 2 June 2024; the amendment to Section 5 makes Amaravati the sole capital from that date.

q.s: In the India Stack, the 'cashless' layer is enabled by:
q.x: Presence-less is Aadhaar authentication, paperless is e-KYC/e-Sign/DigiLocker, cashless is UPI/AePS and consent is the Account Aggregator.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (India Stack layer - enabler) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The presence-less layer is Aadhaar authentication.

q.s: AMRUT, the Smart Cities Mission and PMAY-Urban were launched on:
q.x: These three were launched on 25 June 2015; HRIDAY came on 21 January 2015 and SBM-Urban on 2 October 2014.

q.s: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched on:
q.x: The Jal Jeevan Mission dates from 15 August 2019.

q.s: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (2021) comes under the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
q.x: ABDM is under the Health Ministry and gives citizens an ABHA ID; Andhra Pradesh leads in ABHA coverage.

q.s: The Jagananna Thodu scheme of Andhra Pradesh provided:
o: Rs 10,000 a year to tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins
q.x: Thodu gave petty vendors interest-free loans; Chedodu helped tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins and YSR Navodayam restructured MSME debt.

q.s: The Chandranna Bima scheme of Andhra Pradesh provides:
q.x: Chandranna Bima is an insurance scheme for unorganised workers.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the principal seat of the new High Court of Andhra Pradesh was to be decided by:
q.x: Section 31 left the principal seat to a Presidential order, so the Act itself named no place.

q.s: The replacement level of the total fertility rate (TFR) is generally taken as:
q.x: Replacement fertility is 2.1; India's TFR of about 1.9 is below it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's demography is correct?
o: India's total fertility rate is about 2.5.
India's demographic dividend has already ended.
India's total fertility rate is below the replacement level.
India's dependency ratio is expected to rise steadily over the next decade.
q.x: India's TFR is about 1.9, below the replacement level of 2.1; the dividend is expected to peak around 2030 and the dependency ratio to fall.

q.s: In the Harrod-Domar model, the growth rate of national income equals:
o: The capital-output ratio divided by the saving ratio
The saving ratio multiplied by the capital-output ratio
The saving ratio divided by the capital-output ratio
q.x: g = s/v, so a higher incremental capital-output ratio gives lower growth for the same saving rate.

q.s: According to the concept of carrying capacity, the environment can go on sustaining life only as long as:
o: Extraction stays within regeneration and wastes within its assimilative capacity
All non-renewable resources are left untouched
q.x: When extraction exceeds regeneration and waste exceeds absorptive capacity, carrying capacity is breached.

q.s: The Environmental Kuznets Curve, relating per capita income and environmental degradation, has the shape of:
q.x: Degradation rises at low incomes and falls after a turning point.

q.s: The Kuznets curve was first applied to the environment by:
q.x: Grossman and Krueger (1991) first showed the inverted-U relation for pollution.

q.s: Which of the following tends to increase the number of people living below the poverty line?
q.x: Unemployment adds to the poor, while more investment brings growth and jobs and reduces poverty.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the fiscal measures of the 1991 reforms?
o: Raising public expenditure to stimulate demand
Lowering peak income and corporate tax rates
q.x: In 1991 public expenditure was controlled, the tax net widened and peak tax rates lowered.

q.s: The States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes was reduced from 42 per cent to 41 per cent by the:
q.x: The 14th FC gave 42 per cent; the 15th cut it to 41 per cent, which the 16th retained.

q.s: What vertical share of the divisible pool did the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommend for the States?
q.x: Though 18 of 28 States sought 50 per cent, the 16th FC kept 41 per cent in view of the Union's fiscal needs.

q.s: Under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, Special Category States receive Centre-State funding in the ratio:
q.x: Special Category States get an automatic 90:10 share, and their unspent funds do not lapse.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a benefit given to Special Category States?
o: Automatic 90:10 funding of Centrally Sponsored Schemes
Exemption from the Finance Commission's devolution formula
q.x: SCS States still get devolution through the Finance Commission formula; their benefits include non-lapsable funds, a Rs 10 lakh GST threshold and 90:10 CSS funding.

q.s: Atal Tinkering Labs under the Atal Innovation Mission are set up in:
q.x: Tinkering Labs are for schools; Incubation Centres are for start-ups and Community Innovation Centres for underserved areas.

q.s: The Atal Innovation Mission is run by:
q.x: AIM is NITI Aayog's flagship innovation initiative.

q.s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index 2022?
q.x: Tamil Nadu topped the EPI 2022 (released July 2023); Andhra Pradesh was 8th.

q.s: The SDG India Index is released by:
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
q.x: NITI Aayog brings out the SDG India Index; Andhra Pradesh also has its own localised SDG framework.

q.s: DWCRA (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas) began in 1982-83 as a sub-scheme of:
q.x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of the Integrated Rural Development Programme.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh the SHG model is implemented by:
q.x: The Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty runs the SHG programme; AP leads the country in SHG-bank linkage.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana was launched in:
q.x: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PMJDY accounts is correct?
o: Women hold more than half of the accounts.
Women hold less than one-third of the accounts.
About three-fourths of the accounts are in metro and urban areas.
There are only about 15 crore accounts in all.
q.x: Over half the accounts are held by women, about three-fourths are in rural and semi-urban areas, and there are about 59 crore accounts (14.72 crore was the 2015 figure).

q.s: The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) was introduced by the RBI in:
q.x: The LAF dates from June 2000; the MSF began in May 2011.

q.s: The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate is at present set at:
q.x: The MSF is now repo + 25 bps (it began at repo + 100 bps), with banks able to dip into SLR up to 2 per cent of NDTL.

q.s: The Consumer Price Index (Rural, Urban and Combined) is compiled by the:
o: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
q.x: CPI is compiled by the NSO; the Labour Bureau compiles CPI-IW and the Office of the Economic Adviser the WPI.

q.s: Compared with the 2012-based CPI series, food and beverages in the new CPI (base 2024) carry:
q.x: Food and beverages weigh 36.75 per cent in the new series, less than in the 2012 series.

q.s: Wealth tax in India was abolished in:
q.x: Wealth tax (1957) went in 2015, estate duty in 1985 and gift tax in 1998.

q.s: Which of the following taxes has NOT been abolished in India?
q.x: Estate duty went in 1985, gift tax in 1998 and wealth tax in 2015; STT, introduced in 2004, is still levied.

q.s: In the Gender Budget Statement of the Union Budget, Part A covers schemes in which:
o: 30-99 per cent of the allocation is for women
Less than 30 per cent of the allocation is for women
At least 50 per cent of the allocation is for women
100 per cent of the allocation is for women
q.x: Part A covers 100 per cent schemes, Part B 30-99 per cent and Part C less than 30 per cent.

q.s: The Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), in force from 1 October 2025, is India's agreement with:
q.x: TEPA is with EFTA; ECTA is with Australia, CETA with the UK and CEPA with the UAE.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (trade agreement - partner) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: CETA is with the United Kingdom; ECTA is with Australia.

q.s: A 'direct quote' of an exchange rate expresses:
o: Units of foreign currency per unit of domestic currency
The rate for delivery on a future date
Units of domestic currency per unit of foreign currency
The rate fixed by the IMF
q.x: Rs 95 = $1 is a direct quote; the indirect quote is the reverse.

q.s: White Revolution 2.0 was launched in 2024 by the:
o: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
q.x: White Revolution 2.0, aiming at 75,000 new dairy cooperative societies, is a Ministry of Cooperation initiative.

q.s: What is India's rank among the milk-producing countries of the world?
q.x: India is the largest milk producer, with 239.3 million tonnes in 2023-24.

q.s: e-NAM, the national electronic agricultural market, is implemented by the:
q.x: SFAC launched e-NAM in April 2016; NAFED and NCCF procure under PM-AASHA.

q.s: Operation Greens, announced in the Budget 2018-19, originally covered:
q.x: Operation Greens began with TOP crops and was widened to 22 perishables.

q.s: The Green Revolution in India began with high-yielding varieties of:
q.x: The early phase (1968-81) began with wheat; rice came later.

q.s: The Mexican dwarf wheat varieties used in the Indian Green Revolution were developed by:
q.x: Borlaug's dwarf wheats were grown mainly in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

q.s: The Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme for fertilisers was introduced in:
q.x: NBS began in 2010; neem coating of all urea came in 2015, the DBT pilot in 2016 and PM-PRANAM in 2023.

q.s: PM-PRANAM, approved in 2023, encourages the States to:
o: Reduce the use of chemical fertilisers
q.x: States keep 50 per cent of the subsidy saved by cutting chemical fertiliser use.

q.s: The CRAFICARD (1979-81), whose report led to the setting up of NABARD, was chaired by:
q.x: Sivaraman chaired CRAFICARD; Gorwala the All India Rural Credit Survey, Khusro the 1989 review and Vyas the 2004 committee.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (committee - chairman) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Agricultural Credit Review Committee (1989) - B. Sivaraman
All India Rural Credit Survey - A.D. Gorwala
Flow of Credit to Agriculture (2004) - V.S. Vyas
q.x: The 1989 Agricultural Credit Review Committee was chaired by A.M. Khusro.

q.s: Rythu Bazars, farmers' markets started in 1999, belong to which State?
q.x: Rythu Bazar is AP's; Uzhavar Sandhai is Tamil Nadu's, Apni Mandi Punjab's and Hadapsar Mandi Maharashtra's.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (farmers' market - State) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Apni Mandi belongs to Punjab.

q.s: Which industry carries the lowest weight in the Index of Eight Core Industries?
q.x: Fertilisers have the lowest weight in every series; electricity has the highest in the 2022-23 series, followed by refinery products.

q.s: The share of manufacturing in India's real GVA has stayed at about:
q.x: Manufacturing's real share has held at 17-18 per cent; industry as a whole is about 25 per cent of GVA.

q.s: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) became a separate ministry in:
q.x: MeitY was formed in 2016 from the earlier Department of Electronics and IT (DeitY).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Policy on IT, 2012 is correct?
o: It aimed at software exports of USD 50 billion by 2020.
It was issued after MeitY became a separate ministry.
It aimed at making at least one person in every household e-literate.
It made English the only language of e-governance.
q.x: NPIT 2012 targeted USD 200 billion of software exports and one e-literate person per household; MeitY came only in 2016.

q.s: The Swarna Andhra @2047 vision targets an unemployment rate of below:
q.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 aims at unemployment below 2 per cent and a skilled workforce above 95 per cent.

q.s: Official estimates of unemployment and labour force participation rate (LFPR) for Andhra Pradesh are drawn from the:
q.x: PLFS 2023-24 gave AP's unemployment as 4.1 per cent and LFPR as 47.5 per cent (all ages).

q.s: Under the Special Assistance Measure for Andhra Pradesh, the Centre funds what share of externally aided projects?
q.x: The Centre meets 90 per cent of externally aided projects; the 14th FC gave separate awards for AP and Telangana.

q.s: States' off-budget borrowings, such as through Kerala's KIIFB, are adjusted by the Centre against their:
q.x: Off-budget borrowings lie outside reported debt, so the Centre counts them against the Net Borrowing Ceiling.

q.s: Under the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal award (1980), of the 80 TMC diverted by Polavaram to the Krishna, Andhra Pradesh gets:
q.x: AP gets 45 TMC and the upper States 35 TMC.

q.s: Of the upper riparian share of 35 TMC from the Polavaram diversion, Karnataka gets:
q.x: Karnataka gets 21 TMC and Maharashtra 14 TMC.

q.s: The Godavari River Management Board set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 has its headquarters at:
q.x: The Godavari board is in Telangana (Hyderabad); the boards were constituted by the Central Government.

q.s: The jurisdictions of the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards were notified by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in:
q.x: The jurisdiction notifications were issued in July 2021.

q.s: The 'Grey Revolution' is associated with:
q.x: Grey is fertilisers; Round is potato, Sweet is honey and Pink is meat and poultry.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Honey belongs to the Sweet Revolution; Grey Revolution is fertilisers.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh's district-wise industrial strategy, Nellore district is identified mainly with:
q.x: Nellore: leather, electronics, auto components; Guntur: food processing, cement; Srikakulam: agro, chemicals, petrochemicals; Kadapa: textiles.

q.s: The Orvakal industrial node in Andhra Pradesh is part of which industrial corridor?
q.x: Orvakal is on the HBIC; Krishnapatnam is on the CBIC and Kopparthy on the VCIC.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is being developed with funding mainly from the:
q.x: The VCIC, part of the East Coast Economic Corridor, is ADB-funded.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the core hubs of Andhra Pradesh's e-Pragati architecture?
q.x: e-Pragati's core hubs are People, Land, Entity, GIS and IoT; there is no Finance Hub.

q.s: Computerised land registration in Andhra Pradesh began in 1998 under the project called:
q.x: CARD (Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department) began in 1998; Bhoomi is Karnataka's land-records project.

q.s: The Pole Star (Polaris) lies in which constellation?
q.x: Polaris is in Ursa Minor (the Little Bear).

q.s: Because of the precession of the Earth's axis, which star is expected to become the pole star in about 12,000 years?
q.x: Vega will be close to the celestial north pole in about 12,000 years.

q.s: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following States?
q.x: The Tropic passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, but not Odisha or Manipur; AP lies wholly south of it.

q.s: Leap seconds are added to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) from time to time because:
o: The Earth's orbit is becoming circular
The Earth's rotation is slowing down
The Moon is moving closer to the Earth
q.x: UTC is kept by atomic clocks; leap seconds keep it in step with the slowing Earth, as on 31 December 2016.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a young fold mountain range?
q.x: The Aravallis and Urals are old fold mountains; the Alps, Andes and Rockies are young.

q.s: Cirques, aretes, horns and moraines are landforms made by:
q.x: These are glacial landforms; deltas and gorges are made by rivers.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a landform made by running water?
q.x: A cirque is a glacial landform.

q.s: Which is the largest sea in the world?
q.x: The Philippine Sea is the largest sea.

q.s: Which is regarded as the shallowest sea in the world, only about 14 m deep?
q.x: The Sea of Azov is the shallowest sea.

q.s: The most typical tree of the Mediterranean climatic region is the:
q.x: Olive and cork oak are typical of Mediterranean lands; teak belongs to the tropical monsoon forests.

q.s: Which of the following trees is NOT typical of the Mediterranean region?
q.x: Teak belongs to the tropical monsoon forests.

q.s: Which of the following statements about La Nina is correct?
o: It warms the eastern equatorial Pacific.
It brings warmer winters to North India.
q.x: During La Nina the trade winds strengthen, the eastern Pacific cools, the Walker circulation strengthens and North India gets colder winters.

q.s: The Himalaya extend about 2,400 km from Nanga Parbat in the west to which peak in the east?
q.x: The Himalaya run from Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa and cover about 5 lakh sq km.

q.s: The width of the Himalaya is greatest in:
q.x: The width decreases from about 500 km in Kashmir to about 200 km in Arunachal Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following local names of the Western Ghats lies farthest south?
q.x: From north to south: Sahyadri, Nilgiri, Anaimalai, Palani and Cardamom.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a local name of the Western Ghats?
q.x: Mahendragiri is a peak of the Eastern Ghats in Odisha.

q.s: Which is the largest island of Lakshadweep?
q.x: Andrott is the largest; Kavaratti is the capital and Minicoy the southernmost.

q.s: Minicoy is separated from the rest of the Lakshadweep islands by the:
q.x: The Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the other islands; the Eight Degree Channel lies between Minicoy and the Maldives.

q.s: Red Sanders is endemic to which hill range of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Red Sanders is endemic to the Seshachalam hills; Nallamala has Srisailam and the Chenchus.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (hill range of Andhra Pradesh - feature) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Erramala is the water divide between the Krishna and the Penna; Red Sanders is endemic to Seshachalam.

q.s: The Disaster Management Act of India was enacted in:
q.x: The Disaster Management Act was passed in 2005.

q.s: The IMD treats a year as an all-India drought year when the monsoon rainfall deficiency exceeds:
q.x: An all-India drought year needs a deficiency above 10 per cent with more than 20 per cent of the area affected.

q.s: The Karewa soils of the Kashmir valley, famous for saffron, are:
q.x: Karewas are lake deposits of glacial clay and moraine; saffron is grown at Pampore.

q.s: Which soil order covers the largest share of India's area under the ICAR/USDA classification?
q.x: Inceptisols (about 40 per cent) are the largest order; Mollisols are the smallest.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (soil order - description) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Inceptisols - Largest soil order of India
Mollisols - Smallest soil order of India
q.x: Vertisols are the cracking-clay black soils.

q.s: Which of the following crops is best suited to black (regur) soil?
q.x: Black soil's high moisture retention lets rain-fed cotton last through the dry season.

q.s: In the northern plains, old alluvium is called:
q.x: Bhangar is old alluvium and Khadar new alluvium.

q.s: The India State of Forest Report (ISFR) is published by the:
q.x: The FSI publishes the ISFR every two years; ISFR 2023 put AP's forest cover at about 18.47 per cent of its area.

q.s: Which country is the world's leading producer of maize?
q.x: Maize production is led by the USA, followed by China and Brazil.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT among the world's four leading producers of potato?
q.x: Potato is led by China and India, followed by Russia and Ukraine.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase of the:
q.x: The VCIC is phase one of the ECEC from Kolkata to Kanyakumari; its AP nodes are Visakhapatnam, Chittoor and Kopparthy.

q.s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor?
q.x: The DMIC covers Delhi, UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat and Maharashtra.

q.s: The Alang-Sosiya ship-breaking yard is located in:
q.x: Alang-Sosiya is in Bhavnagar district of Gujarat.

q.s: Which is regarded as the largest shipyard in India?
q.x: Cochin Shipyard is the largest; Hindustan Shipyard is at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: The proposed 'A.P. Drone City' is located in which district?
q.x: Drone City is at Kurnool; Space City is in Tirupati and the Veldurthi Mega Textile Park in Palnadu.

q.s: The headquarters of the South Coast Railway zone is at:
