q.x: South Coast Railway is headquartered at Visakhapatnam; South Central Railway kept Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Nanded divisions.

q.s: After the formation of the South Coast Railway, the remaining part of the Waltair division became the Rayagada division of the:
q.x: The rest of Waltair went to the new Rayagada division of the East Coast Railway.

q.s: The LEADS (Logistics Ease Across Different States) report is brought out by the:
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
q.x: LEADS is prepared by the Commerce Ministry (DPIIT); in LEADS 2025 Tamil Nadu led the coastal States.

q.s: The six-digit PIN code was introduced in India on:
q.x: The PIN code began on 15 August 1972.

q.s: How many regional PIN zones are there in India, apart from the zone for the Army Postal Service?
q.x: There are eight regional zones and a ninth for the Army Postal Service.

q.s: The GI-tagged Etikoppaka lacquer toys, coloured with natural dyes, belong to which district?
q.x: Etikoppaka is in Anakapalli district; Kondapalli toys belong to NTR district.

q.s: The Sri City SEZ is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Sri City is in Tirupati district; APSEZ is in Anakapalli.

q.s: The Pydibhimavaram pharma cluster is located in which district?
q.x: Pydibhimavaram is in Srikakulam district.

q.s: In the UNDP Human Development Report, the 'High' human development category begins at an HDI value of:
q.x: High starts at 0.700; India's 0.685 places it in the Medium band (0.550-0.699).

q.s: In the Human Development Report 2025, India is placed in which category?
q.x: India's HDI of 0.685 is in the Medium category.

q.s: Swarna Andhra @2047 targets a GSDP of:
q.x: It also targets a per capita income above USD 43,000 and 100 per cent literacy.

q.s: According to NFHS-5 (2019-21), India's overall sex ratio (females per 1,000 males) was:
q.x: NFHS-5 recorded 1,020, the first time above 1,000 in any NFHS; NFHS-4 was 991 and the urban figure 985.

q.s: Which State recorded the lowest literacy rate in Census 2011?
q.x: Bihar had the lowest literacy (about 62 per cent) in 2011.

q.s: Which of the following statements about literacy in Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011) is correct?
o: AP's female literacy fell between 2001 and 2011.
AP's gender gap in literacy was narrower than the national gap.
AP had the lowest literacy among the States.
AP's literacy was below 40 per cent.
q.x: AP's literacy rose to 67.35 per cent, female literacy to 59.96 per cent, and its gap of about 15 points was below India's 16; Bihar was the lowest.

q.s: The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (RECS) Act, 1979 has been merged into the:
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
q.x: The 1979 Act, which applied to establishments with five or more inter-State migrants, is now part of the OSH Code.

q.s: Under the Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979, the displacement allowance payable to a migrant worker was:
q.x: The Act provided a displacement allowance of 50 per cent of monthly wages.

q.s: The difference between rural and urban population growth rates in India is mainly due to:
q.x: Natural increase differs little between rural and urban areas, so migration explains the gap.

q.s: Nepali, a language of the Eighth Schedule, is also an official language of which State?
q.x: Nepali is an official language of Sikkim; English has never been in the Eighth Schedule.

q.s: Gor Boli, which has been demanded for the Eighth Schedule, is spoken by which community of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Gor Boli is the language of the Banjara/Sugali (Lambada) community.

q.s: Which is the largest language family of the world by number of speakers?
q.x: Indo-European has the most speakers, followed by Sino-Tibetan.

q.s: Which language family has the largest number of languages?
q.x: Niger-Congo, which includes the Bantu languages, has the most languages.

q.s: The national database of unorganised workers launched by the Ministry of Labour is called:
q.x: Over 31 crore unorganised workers are registered on e-Shram, 54 per cent of them women.

q.s: Which sector has the largest share in India's Gross Value Added?
q.x: The tertiary sector accounts for over half (about 52.9 per cent) of India's GVA.

q.s: Coral reefs are absent in the Gulf of Khambhat mainly because of:
q.x: Corals need clear, saline water; the silt and fresh water entering the Gulf of Khambhat prevent reef growth.

q.s: Which of the following have been declared India's 'Hope Spots' for marine conservation?
o: Lakshadweep and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands
Gulf of Mannar and Gulf of Kachchh
q.x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands are India's Hope Spots.

q.s: How many Biosphere Reserves are there in India?
q.x: India has 18 Biosphere Reserves, 58 Tiger Reserves and 33 Elephant Reserves.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of protected area under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972?
q.x: Biosphere Reserves come under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere programme, not the WPA.

q.s: Gahirmatha on the Odisha coast is famous as a mass-nesting site of:
q.x: Olive ridleys nest in large numbers at Gahirmatha; Turtle Excluder Devices and seasonal fishing bans protect them from trawler nets.

q.s: Turtle Excluder Devices are fitted to:
q.x: TEDs let turtles escape from the nets of mechanised trawlers.

q.s: Papikonda, a wildlife sanctuary from 1978, was declared a National Park in:
q.x: Papikonda became a National Park in 2008 and after 2014 lies wholly in Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: Papikonda National Park lies along which river?
q.x: The park covers the Papikondalu hills along the Godavari gorge.

q.s: Which State produces about 71 per cent of India's coffee?
q.x: Karnataka is the leading coffee producer; AP (Araku) is 4th, and Kerala leads in natural rubber.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in the production of all the following EXCEPT:
q.x: AP leads in oil palm, papaya, cocoa and chillies; Karnataka leads in arecanut.

q.s: The Academy of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is located at:
q.x: The NDRF, raised in 2006 under Section 44 of the DM Act, has its Academy at Nagpur.

q.s: The NDRF regional headquarters for Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka is at:
q.x: The regional headquarters for the three States is at Vijayawada.

q.s: Planting mangroves and shelter belts along the coast is a mitigation measure mainly against:
q.x: Mangroves and shelter belts break the force of cyclonic winds and storm surges; earthquakes are met through building codes.

q.s: Retaining walls and regulation of settlements on slopes are mitigation measures mainly for:
q.x: Landslide mitigation includes retaining walls, regulating settlements and hazard zonation; floods call for desilting, check dams and levees.

q.s: Who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930, the first Asian to win a science Nobel?
q.x: Raman won alone for the Raman Effect; Ross won Medicine in 1902 and Chandrasekhar Physics in 1983.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (laureate - Nobel Prize) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Khorana shared the 1968 Medicine prize for work on the genetic code.

q.s: The Technology Policy Statement of India was issued in:
q.x: The Technology Policy Statement (1983) followed the Scientific Policy Resolution of 1958.

q.s: Which policy first added 'Innovation' to India's science and technology policy?
q.x: The 2013 policy was the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy; the Draft STIP 2020 is the fifth.

q.s: Which of the following was set up earliest?
q.x: TIFR 1945, AEET 1954 (now BARC), AERB 1983, NPCIL 1987.

q.s: The Indian Bureau of Mines is headquartered at:
q.x: The IBM is at Nagpur; Dhanbad has the Indian School of Mines (IIT-ISM).

q.s: The National Policy on Electronics, 2019 targeted electronics manufacturing of US$ 400 billion by:
q.x: NPE 2019 aimed at US$ 400 billion and 1 billion handsets a year by 2025.

q.s: Green hydrogen is produced by:
o: Electrolysis of water using renewable electricity
Steam reforming of natural gas with carbon capture
q.x: Green hydrogen uses renewable power; grey comes from natural gas, brown from coal and blue from gas with carbon capture.

q.s: Green hydrogen is seen as a key option for decarbonising steel and fertiliser plants because:
o: Direct electrification is difficult in these sectors
These sectors already run on solar power
These sectors emit no carbon dioxide
q.x: Steel, fertiliser and refinery units are hard-to-abate sectors.

q.s: State Climate Change Centres that support the State Action Plans on Climate Change are set up under which national mission?
o: National Mission on Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change
National Mission for a Green India
q.x: The NMSKCC supports State Climate Change Centres; 34 SAPCCs are operational.

q.s: India's online single-window platform for drone permissions is called:
q.x: DigitalSky handles drone permissions; the drone PLI scheme (2021) has an outlay of Rs 120 crore.

q.s: Liquid hydrogen used in cryogenic rocket engines is stored at about:
q.x: Liquid hydrogen is kept at about -253 degrees C and liquid oxygen at about -183 degrees C; cryogenic propulsion gives the highest specific impulse.

q.s: In solid rocket propellant, ammonium perchlorate acts as the:
q.x: Ammonium perchlorate is the oxidiser, aluminium powder the fuel and HTPB the binder.

q.s: In solid rocket propellant, HTPB serves as the:
q.x: HTPB (hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene) binds the propellant grain.

q.s: A rocket can move forward in the vacuum of space because of:
q.x: The expelled gases push the rocket forward; it does not need air to push against.

q.s: The Energy Storage Obligation of 2022, rising from 1 per cent in 2023-24 to 4 per cent in 2029-30, was issued by the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
q.x: The Ministry of Power issued the ESO; the CEA puts the storage need at 336 GWh by 2029-30.

q.s: Who was the Project Director of SLV-3, India's first satellite launch vehicle?
q.x: Kalam directed SLV-3, which put Rohini into orbit in 1980.

q.s: The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) was set up under the leadership of:
q.x: Sarabhai chaired INCOSPAR, set up TERLS and founded PRL and IIM Ahmedabad.

q.s: Which ISRO launch vehicle has three solid stages and a liquid Velocity Trimming Module?
q.x: SSLV uses three solid stages plus a VTM; SLV-3 had four solid stages and ASLV five.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (launch vehicle - stages) is NOT correctly matched?
o: SSLV - Three solid stages and a liquid VTM
q.x: ASLV had five all-solid stages.

q.s: Agnibaan SOrTeD, launched on 30 May 2024 with a 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine, belongs to:
q.x: Agnibaan is Agnikul's; Skyroot built Vikram-S.

q.s: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S mission 'Prarambh' (2022) was a:
q.x: Vikram-S reached about 89.5 km on a suborbital flight.

q.s: Which of the following statements about satellite orbits is correct?
o: The apogee is the point of an orbit nearest to the Earth.
A geostationary satellite completes one orbit every 12 hours.
A geostationary satellite orbits over the equator and appears fixed in the sky.
A sun-synchronous orbit lies over the equator at about 36,000 km.
q.x: A geostationary satellite circles the equator once a day; apogee is the farthest point and perigee the nearest; sun-synchronous orbits are near-polar.

q.s: A satellite that passes over a given place at the same local solar time each day is in a:
q.x: Sun-synchronous orbits are used for remote-sensing satellites.

q.s: The first Space Shuttle flight, STS-1 (1981), was made by:
q.x: Columbia flew STS-1; Atlantis flew the last mission, STS-135, in 2011.

q.s: The last Space Shuttle mission, STS-135 (2011), was flown by:
q.x: Atlantis ended the shuttle programme in July 2011.

q.s: The Arjun main battle tank was developed by which DRDO laboratory?
q.x: The Combat Vehicles R&D Establishment developed the Arjun and Muntra, DRDO's first unmanned tank.

q.s: Digital Signature Certificates in India are issued by:
o: The Controller of Certifying Authorities directly
Certifying Authorities licensed by the CCA
q.x: The CCA licenses Certifying Authorities, which issue the certificates.

q.s: The technology-neutral term 'electronic signature' was introduced into the IT Act by the amendment of:
q.x: The IT (Amendment) Act, 2008 brought in 'electronic signature' and new offences such as video voyeurism.

q.s: PET imaging mainly uses which radiopharmaceutical?
q.x: F-18 FDG is made in cyclotrons such as the 30 MeV Medical Cyclotron, Kolkata.

q.s: Radiation treatment with an external Cobalt-60 beam is called:
q.x: Teletherapy uses an external beam; brachytherapy places a sealed source inside or near the tumour.

q.s: The Green Day-Ahead Market on India's power exchanges began in:
q.x: The Green Day-Ahead Market started in 2021; the Real-Time Market began in 2020.

q.s: Biogas is produced from organic matter by:
q.x: Biogas forms by biomethanation in the absence of oxygen; the leftover slurry is a good manure.

q.s: The main constituent of biogas is:
q.x: Biogas is mostly methane with carbon dioxide.

q.s: In India, the upper limit of a small hydro project is:
q.x: Small hydro is up to 25 MW; micro is up to 100 kW and mini from 101 kW to 2 MW.

q.s: In India, micro hydro plants have a capacity of up to:
q.x: Micro hydro plants are up to 100 kW.

q.s: Which State leads India in installed solar power capacity?
q.x: Rajasthan leads in solar, while Gujarat leads in total renewable capacity and in wind.

q.s: India's installed wind power capacity crossed 50 GW in:
q.x: Capacity was 21 GW in 2014, 39 GW in 2021 and 42 GW in July 2023, crossing 50 GW in March 2025.

q.s: The invasive Prosopis juliflora has degraded which grassland of Gujarat?
q.x: Prosopis juliflora has spread over the Banni grasslands and lowers groundwater in Rayalaseema.

q.s: The Sangai (brow-antlered deer) is found in:
q.x: The Sangai lives on the floating phumdis of Keibul Lamjao; the Hangul is at Dachigam.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (species - habitat) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Hangul (Kashmir stag) lives in Dachigam; Gir is home to the Asiatic lion.

q.s: Which section of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 lets the Centre notify a non-Schedule I animal as vermin?
q.x: Section 62 covers vermin; Section 9 prohibits hunting and Section 11 permits killing of dangerous animals with the Chief Wildlife Warden's permission.

q.s: The National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the:
q.x: The PM chairs the NBWL; a State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Chief Minister.

q.s: The National Biodiversity Authority is headquartered at:
q.x: The NBA is at Chennai; the Animal Welfare Board moved to Ballabhgarh, Haryana in 2018.

q.s: The National Forest Policy, 1988 aims to bring what share of the country's area under forest or tree cover?
q.x: The 1988 policy aims at one-third of the country and two-thirds of the hills.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a forest class under the National Forest Policy, 1952?
q.x: The 1952 classes were protection forests, national forests, village forests and tree lands.

q.s: Which is the largest source of India's greenhouse gas emissions?
q.x: Energy, mainly coal power, is the largest source.

q.s: India's per capita CO2 emission is about:
q.x: At about 2 tonnes, India's per capita emission is the lowest in the G20, though India is the third-largest total emitter.

q.s: India's draft rules for labelling GM food, with a 1 per cent threshold, were issued by the:
q.x: FSSAI issued the draft labelling rules; the BRAI Bill (2013) lapsed without being passed.

q.s: India's BioE3 Policy (2024) stands for:
o: Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment
Bioenergy for Equity, Efficiency and Exports
Biodiversity for Ecology, Economy and Ethics
Biomedicine for Education, Equity and Employment
q.x: BioE3 proposes single-window clearance and regulatory sandboxes for biomanufacturing.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four classic criteria of hazardous waste?
q.x: The four criteria are ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity and toxicity.

q.s: According to the WHO, about what share of healthcare waste is hazardous?
q.x: About 85 per cent of healthcare waste is general, non-hazardous waste; about 15 per cent is hazardous.

q.s: The main aim of Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 (2021-26) is to make all cities:
q.x: SBM-U 2.0, launched on 1 October 2021 with about Rs 1.41 lakh crore, aims at Garbage Free cities.

q.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban is run by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
q.x: SBM-U (2 October 2014) is under MoHUA; SBM-Gramin is under Jal Shakti.

q.s: The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 came into force on:
q.x: The 2022 Rules took effect on 1 April 2023 and cover 106 EEE items.

q.s: The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 do NOT apply to:
q.x: Radioactive waste and packaging plastics have their own rules; solar PV waste is covered.

q.s: Which of the following is a secondary air pollutant?
q.x: Ozone and ammonium sulphate form in the air from other pollutants; lead from vehicles is a primary pollutant. Ground-level ozone harms lungs and plants.

q.s: Which of the following statements about air pollutants is correct?
o: Lead emitted from vehicles is a primary pollutant.
Ground-level ozone is beneficial to lungs and plants.
Ammonium sulphate is emitted directly from vehicle exhausts.
Secondary pollutants are emitted directly from their sources.
q.x: Primary pollutants come directly from sources; ammonium sulphate and ozone form in the air, and ground-level ozone is harmful.

q.s: The Environmental Impact Assessment notification currently governing project clearances in India was issued in:
q.x: The EIA Notification of 2006 replaced the 1994 notification; a 2020 draft was not finalised.

q.s: India became the third country to set up a specialised environmental tribunal, after Australia and:
q.x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010 and the Tribunal began work in July 2011.

q.s: The National Green Tribunal Act was passed in:
q.x: The Act dates from 2010; the NGT started functioning in 2011.

q.s: The Minamata Convention deals with:
o: Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals
q.x: Minamata (2013) is on mercury; Basel is on hazardous wastes, Rotterdam on PIC and Stockholm on POPs.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (convention - subject) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Rotterdam deals with Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides.

q.s: In recombinant DNA technology, DNA fragments such as a gene and a vector are joined by:
q.x: Ligase joins fragments; restriction endonucleases cut at specific recognition sequences.

q.s: A plasmid used as a vector in genetic engineering is:
o: A protein coat of a virus
q.x: Plasmids are circular double-stranded DNA; in pBR322, 'BR' stands for Bolivar and Rodriguez.

q.s: Biopesticides are a key part of Integrated Pest Management because they are:
o: Persistent in the soil for years
q.x: Biopesticides break down quickly and are low in toxicity; they do not persist in the soil.

q.s: Germanwatch, which publishes the Climate Risk Index, is based in:
q.x: Germanwatch is a Bonn-based organisation; it also co-publishes the CCPI.

q.s: Which is India's first marine biosphere reserve?
q.x: The Gulf of Mannar was India's first marine biosphere reserve.

q.s: The coral reefs of Lakshadweep are entirely:
q.x: Lakshadweep has only atolls; the Andaman & Nicobar reefs are the most diverse and the Gulf of Kutch reefs among the most northerly.

q.s: The Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park is located in:
q.x: The Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park (1980) is in Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The symbiotic algae that give reef-building corals their food and colour are called:
q.x: Zooxanthellae live in coral tissue; their loss causes coral bleaching.

q.s: The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is published by:
o: UNEP and the World Meteorological Organization
Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and CAN International
q.x: CCPI is brought out by Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network.

q.s: In the Climate Change Performance Index, the top three ranks are:
o: Given to the three largest economies
Given to the three lowest emitters
q.x: No country is judged good enough for the top three ranks, so they are left empty.

q.s: India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) are approved by the:
q.x: NDCs are prepared by the MoEFCC and approved by the Union Cabinet.

q.s: Under its updated NDC (August 2022), India pledged to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP from 2005 levels by 2030 by:
q.x: The updated NDC raised the pledge to 45 per cent and set 50 per cent non-fossil capacity, adding Mission LiFE.

q.s: Lymphatic filariasis is caused by:
q.x: Filariasis is caused by the roundworm Wuchereria bancrofti; its chronic stage is elephantiasis.

q.s: In India, lymphatic filariasis is transmitted mainly by the:
q.x: Culex is the vector, not the cause; sandflies transmit kala-azar.

q.s: The HPV vaccine protects mainly against:
q.x: A free HPV vaccination campaign for 14-year-old girls was launched in February 2026; cancer is not yet a nationally notifiable disease.

q.s: Which of the following statements about cancer in India is correct?
o: Cancer is a nationally notifiable disease.
Cancer is not a nationally notifiable disease, though several States have notified it.
Cancer cases are projected to fall by 2045.
q.x: Seventeen States have notified cancer; cases are projected to rise from 1.41 million (2022) to 2.46 million (2045).

q.s: In the Lancet study 'Nations within a nation' (2017), Kerala was placed in which Epidemiological Transition Level group?
q.x: Kerala is in the high ETL group and Karnataka in the higher-middle; a low ratio of communicable to NCD DALYs means a high ETL.

q.s: India's first indigenous mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, Gemcovac-OM, was developed by:
q.x: Gemcovac-OM is Gennova's; Covaxin is Bharat Biotech's with ICMR-NIV.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (COVID-19 vaccine - developer) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Covaxin was developed by Bharat Biotech with ICMR-NIV.

q.s: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides health cover of up to how much per family per year?
q.x: PM-JAY gives Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care.

q.s: For most States, the Centre and the State share the cost of PM-JAY in the ratio:
q.x: The ratio is 60:40, and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

q.s: Anaemia Mukt Bharat, following the 6x6x6 strategy, mainly targets:
q.x: Anaemia Mukt Bharat (2018) tackles iron-deficiency anaemia.

q.s: The Janani Suraksha Yojana mainly promotes:
q.x: JSY, a 100 per cent centrally sponsored scheme, gives cash help to promote institutional deliveries.

q.s: The BharatNet project aims to provide broadband connectivity to:
q.x: BharatNet reaches about 2.18 lakh gram panchayats but not yet every village.

q.s: Which of the following statements about BRICS is correct?
o: Its permanent secretariat is in New Delhi.
Its presidency is held permanently by China.
It has no permanent secretariat or headquarters.
q.x: BRICS has no secretariat; India's 2026 presidency marks 20 years of BRICS, with the theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.

q.s: The headquarters of the International Solar Alliance is at:
q.x: The ISA is headquartered at Gurugram.

q.s: The International Solar Alliance aims to mobilise solar investment of how much by 2030?
q.x: The ISA mobilises investment and supports policy; it does not build plants itself.

q.s: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) is built on the:
q.x: GERD, of 5,150 MW, is on the Blue Nile and was inaugurated by Abiy Ahmed.

q.s: The 47th ASEAN Summit, held along with the 22nd ASEAN-India Summit in October 2025, took place at:
q.x: Malaysia hosted it at Kuala Lumpur with the theme 'Inclusivity and Sustainability'.

q.s: 2026 has been designated the ASEAN-India Year of:
q.x: 2026 is the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation.

q.s: At the G20 Johannesburg Summit (2025), India's 'Africa Skills Multiplier' initiative envisages:
o: One million engineers in five years
One million trainers in a decade
q.x: India also proposed an Open Satellite Data Partnership and, with Brazil and South Africa, a Digital Innovation Alliance.

q.s: Horizon Europe, the current EU framework programme for research and innovation, runs from:
q.x: The ERC and Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions fall under its first pillar; India concluded association talks only in November 2026.

q.s: The US Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) is:
o: A labour certification issued by the US Department of Labor
A visa that directly grants permanent residence
q.x: PERM is a step towards an employment-based green card and is valid for 180 days.

q.s: Under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), duty-free access in the UK covers about what share of Indian products?
q.x: CETA, in force from 15 July 2026, gives duty-free access to 99 per cent of Indian products, not all.

q.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement is the second instrument adopted under Article 19 of the WHO Constitution. The first was the:
q.x: The FCTC (2003) was the first treaty under Article 19; the IHR are regulations under Article 21.

q.s: Which of the following commodities is NOT covered by the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?
q.x: The EUDR covers cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood.

q.s: The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which concerns Indian exporters, covers products such as:
q.x: CBAM covers carbon-intensive goods such as steel, aluminium, cement and fertilisers.

q.s: Under the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project, cargo from Kolkata goes by sea to which Myanmar port before moving on to Mizoram?
q.x: Cargo goes Kolkata-Sittwe by sea, then by river and road; the Paletwa-Zorinpui road is still unfinished.

q.s: Which became the first Arab country to bar children under 15 from creating social media accounts?
q.x: The UAE was the first Arab country to do so.

q.s: India's Act East Policy, under which Vietnam is a key partner, was launched in:
q.x: The Look East Policy (1991) became the Act East Policy in 2014.

q.s: Who became Interim President of Venezuela after US forces seized President Nicolas Maduro in January 2026?
q.x: Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores were seized; Vice-President Delcy Rodriguez became Interim President. The UN Secretary-General called it a dangerous precedent.

q.s: Under the India-UK deals during PM Keir Starmer's visit (October 2025), India's first assembly and testing facility in Hyderabad is for which missile?
q.x: ASRAAM gets a Hyderabad facility; the LMM deal (GBP 350 million) is for missiles made in Belfast.

q.s: ISRO's semi-cryogenic SC120 stage will replace which stage of the LVM3?
q.x: The SC120 stage, developed after the Power Head Test Article tests at IPRC Mahendragiri, will replace the L110.

q.s: ISRO's semi-cryogenic Power Head Test Article was hot-tested at:
q.x: The test was at the ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri.

q.s: The Light Combat Aircraft Tejas was designed by the:
q.x: Tejas was designed by ADA and is built by HAL.

q.s: No. 17 Squadron 'Golden Arrows' of the Indian Air Force now flies the:
q.x: The Golden Arrows, raised at Ambala in 1951, fly the Rafale.

q.s: Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX is a joint lunar mission of ISRO with:
q.x: LUPEX is with Japan's JAXA; in TRISHNA, France's CNES provides the thermal infrared instrument.

q.s: Under Space Vision 2047, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted by:
q.x: The space station is targeted by 2035 and an Indian crewed lunar landing by 2040.

q.s: Which country amended its Constitution to protect mental integrity against misuse of neurotechnology?
q.x: Chile was the first to protect 'neurorights' in its Constitution; California passed a brain-data law in 2024.

q.s: The Namo Drone Didi scheme provides drones to:
q.x: Namo Drone Didi gives drones to women SHGs for agricultural services.

q.s: The SVAMITVA scheme uses drones to map:
q.x: SVAMITVA surveys village abadi areas and gives property cards.

q.s: Adult neurogenesis in humans has been confirmed in which part of the brain?
q.x: Single-cell RNA sequencing with AI confirmed new neurons in the hippocampal dentate gyrus.

q.s: The hypothalamus forms part of the:
q.x: The hypothalamus is the basal part of the diencephalon.

q.s: Exercise Konkan is a naval exercise between India and:
q.x: Konkan-25 was the first India-UK Carrier Strike Group exercise, with INS Vikrant and HMS Prince of Wales; Varuna is with France.

q.s: Tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean are named by:
o: RSMC New Delhi, run by the IMD
q.x: RSMC New Delhi names them from a list of 13 names each from the 13 member countries of the WMO/ESCAP Panel.

q.s: The World Meteorological Organization is headquartered at:
q.x: The WMO is in Geneva; Nairobi is the UNEP headquarters.

q.s: India is the world's third-largest generator of e-waste, after:
q.x: India ranks third after China and the USA; it is a party to the Basel Convention.

q.s: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 prohibit:
o: Landfilling and incineration of waste batteries
Recycling of batteries by private firms
q.x: Waste batteries may not be landfilled or incinerated.

q.s: The 2021-25 DNA-based Synchronous All-India Elephant Estimation was carried out by the:
q.x: The WII estimate put the population at 22,446, against 27,312 in 2017.

q.s: The gestation period of an elephant is about:
q.x: Elephants have the longest gestation of land mammals, 18-22 months.

q.s: Under source segregation of household waste, the green bin is meant for:
q.x: Green is wet, blue dry, red sanitary (wrapped separately) and black special-care waste.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (bin colour - waste stream) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The blue bin is for dry waste.

q.s: The World Air Quality Report is released by:
q.x: IQAir brings out the report; in 2025 Loni in Uttar Pradesh was the most polluted city.

q.s: According to the World Air Quality Report 2025, the most polluted city in the world was:
q.x: Loni (Uttar Pradesh) was the most polluted city; Pakistan was the most polluted country.

q.s: Coral bleaching, in which corals turn white, occurs mainly when:
o: Heat stress makes corals expel their zooxanthellae
q.x: Under heat stress corals expel their symbiotic algae and lose colour; they can still recover.

q.s: The UNHCR, set up in 1950, is headquartered at:
q.x: UNHCR is in Geneva; its Global Trends report showed forced displacement falling to 117.8 million in 2025.

q.s: Which organisation estimated that work-related stress causes about 840,000 deaths a year, costing about 1.37 per cent of global GDP?
